title: Structure of Capsid of Stx-converting Bacteriophage phi24B Obtained by Cryo-EM and Local Reconstructions
content: Escherichia coli is an indigenous bacterial symbiont in the intestines of several vertebrates, including humans, nevertheless, many E.coli strains can cause infections. Among them Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC), known as dangerous food-born pathogen, inducing severe hemorrhagic colitis. STEC gains toxigenic phenotype due to the lysogenic conversion by Shiga toxin-encoding phages (Stx phages). However, the toxin is produced only during the lytic cycle of the virus. In addition, Stx phages may improve fitness of the lysogen in the gut. Although the global incidence of STEC infection is low, severe disease is observed in about 10% of affected individuals with a mortality rate of 3–5%. The toxin production depends on the in situ induction level in the pathogen’s population developed in a patient. Therefore the usage of antibiotics increasing the prophage induction is not recommended for the STEC infection treatement.
